text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the baby was born and if they passed their first stool (meconium) within the first 48 hours of life? Also, is there any family history of genetic conditions like cystic fibrosis?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was the baby fed any formula or breast milk before the vomiting started, or was this purely due to obstruction? I need to determine if there are any signs of peritonitis or sepsis. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

text: Given the failure to pass meconium and the X-ray findings, I suspect Hirschsprung's disease. Does the baby have any other symptoms like fever, lethargy, or poor feeding that might suggest enterocolitis? REQUEST TEST: Rectal Suction Biopsy
